title: Expected Number of Shared Birthday Pairs

problemStatement.formal: E[pairs] = C(n,2)/d for n people with d possible birthdays. Generalizes to E[k-tuples] = C(n,k)/d^(k-1). The first n where E[pairs] > 1 is n=28 (d=365). The first n where E[triples] > 1 is n=94. The first n where E[quads] > 1 is n=188.
problemStatement.plain: Formalize the expected number of shared birthday pairs, triples, and k-tuples among n people with d equally likely birthdays, including threshold computations for the standard 365-day calendar.
whyMatters: Extends the classic Birthday Problem from probability of any match to expected count of matches
Demonstrates linearity of expectation in formal mathematics
Generalizes from pairs to k-tuples with precise threshold computations
Connects combinatorics (binomial coefficients) with probability theory

proven: expectedPairs_succ: additivity (each new person adds n/d)
thresholds_summary: unified summary of all thresholds

insights: linearity of expectation reduces to C(n,k)/d^(k-1) formula
Threshold n for E[k-tuples] > 1 grows roughly as (k!*d^(k-1))^(1/k)
Variance <= Expected because (d-1)/d <= 1 for indicator-based variance
Combinatorial identity 3*C(n,3) = C(n,2)*(n-2) connects pairs and triples
